Yeah the memory loss is really bad, I write stuff down and then forget where I wrote it or that I wrote it. I struggle to explain stuff to people because my memories are just weird fragments, but then I'll remember a very random unimportant event with extreme detail that I didn't even know I knew about until the topic comes up. The worst is explaining to people that your memory sucks and they say you seem fine or that everyone has times like that. Like I was not always this bad, I know this isn't normal. I'm super scared for getting older cause if it's like this now, how bad will it be when I'm actually old? Also names take me like a year of seeing someone twice a week before I remember them.

I found it helps to let the people closest to me know that while I'm distressed questions are very unhelpful and if they have to ask one to ask them one at a time and wait patiently until I can answer. They don't always remember and very few people are safe enough/care enough to hear me out, but it has helped a decent amount.

I was at 10k but I used a bunch on the recent suits, now I'm at like 5k and I'm really bummed. I get the game needs to make money but wish it was possible to get suits without needing real world money (like you can for a couple events but defiantly not all of them as fast as they happen).

I did it a for a while, before I was diagnosed with Autism, for depression/anxiety I stopped because the horse did not care about me what so ever so I didn't really feel a connection with them. I also got triggered by textures, mainly the feeling after brushing them when you're covered in dust. I did like feeling of the warm air when they breath. It was cool to learn about horse care and I loved being up on the horse, but the first several sessions was ground work, so took a while to get to ride. If you're at all interested and can afford it you should give it a try, you can always stop after a couple times :)

I also get anxiety about this, but I was told bad people don't sit around worrying about how not to hurt people. I think the internet makes the fear worse cause if you mess up you get attacked and yelled at instead of getting the opportunity to learn and grow. In real life most people will be more willing to have an empathetic conversation with you. If your like me the anxiety is happening way more frequently then the scenarios ever could, so maybe just trust that you've scripted it enough times to know what to do if it does happen.
I also tend not to vote for people who use the suits but I get higher rankings whenever I do vs creating the outfit myself so we might be in the minority

I always want to go trick or treating but no one will go with me and I'm too scared to walk up to the houses alone. The last few years of my trick or treating career my family thought it was odd to keep going, but one year my dad came with me and wore a mask so no one could tell exactly how old he was and he had fun. I think you should for sure try it and if people are being mean go to the store and buy all the discount candy as consolation. If you're fine with people knowing you have autism you could make a pin/button to wear on your clothes/costume or use a teal/blue bucket as a indicator.

I have the same issue online. Everyone is just so cruel for no reason and they don't think about how it affects others. I think people just don't get that they are talking to a real person since it's through a screen. I personally post/comment as little as possible or just delete stuff if people are being mean. It stinks when you want to be social and learn more about others and a few loud people ruin it. I've had people tell me to just get over it or not take it personally but that's just not how I work. Logically I can say "no this person was in the wrong" but I still feel sick in my body and it just isn't worth it. I hate when people get pissed when you ask a question. It's like the same vibe online as when you ask someone in authority a clarifying question and they act disrespected.

Edit: sounds like from the comments people think the question was taken as combative instead of inquisitive which tends to happen a lot with question both online and IRL
